short: Joint cell-type ID, then cross-modal prediction
why: Objective names classification first, prediction second; labels stay a yardstick
decision: Primary: integration/classification on label_fine (17 classes; label as secondary), headline = linear-probe balanced accuracy of joint vs RNA alone vs ATAC alone vs early fusion. Secondary: cross-modal prediction rna->atac (binary_top10000, AUROC) and atac->rna (log1p_hvg2000, per-sample/per-feature Pearson r) vs train-mean baseline and single-modality baseline. No labels in training (label-free clip/vicreg). Success: joint probe bal-acc on label_fine >= best single modality, paired-difference 95% CI excluding or including 0 (>= means CI lower bound > -0.02 and no significant loss); if CI includes 0 the verdict is no measurable gain. Prediction: per-sample r / AUROC clearly above train-mean baseline. Change course if joint < best single modality by a paired CI excluding 0.
evidence: profile.json: 8 coarse / 17 fine classes; test classes <10 cells: pDC 7, Plasma 6, CD16- NK 5, Megakaryocyte 2 (uninterpretable individually); n_train 7285; labels from CellTypist on RNA only (DATA.md) so favour RNA
alternatives_rejected: supcon_clip: labels not allowed for training by objective; clustering metrics: not asked

short: Standard RNA and ATAC reductions, plus targets
why: RNA is overdispersed counts; ATAC is near-binary, so each gets its usual treatment
decision: rna: log1p_hvg2000_pca50 (encoder input); atac: tfidf_lsi50_drop1 (encoder input, 49 dims; depth corr of first component r=0.86 so drop1 kept). Targets: rna log1p_hvg2000, atac binary_top10000.
evidence: profile.json: rna 68% nonzeros =1, overdispersion 1.23; atac 72% nonzeros <=2, 91.8% zeros; atac__tfidf_lsi50_drop1.json first_component_corr_with_depth 0.856, explained var 0.067
alternatives_rejected: pca100/lsi100: only if fine-label probe is weak

short: Compare aligned CLIP against simple PCA baselines
why: Prediction needs a shared space; baselines show whether learning helps
decision: Baselines: rna_only_pca, atac_only_pca (pca_concat single input), early_fusion_pca (pca_concat both). Primary: clip with mlp encoders, dim 32, label-free. Alternative: vicreg mlp dim 32 (n_train 7285, many look-alike cells of same type -> false negatives under InfoNCE).
evidence: profile.json n_train 7285; 17 fine classes -> dim 32; objective includes cross-modal prediction
alternatives_rejected: supcon_clip: labels not allowed; simclr: single modality only

short: Default settings sized to 7k training cells
why: Inputs are small, so overfitting rather than time is the risk
decision: clip_mlp_d32: batch 512, lr 1e-3, hidden 256, 2 layers, dropout 0.1, wd 1e-4, select-by val_loss, max 8 min. vicreg_mlp_d32: batch 256, same else, max 5 min. Smoke tests ran OK. Total reserved 13 of 20 min; 7 kept for iterations.
evidence: training skill defaults; n_train 7285; smoke runs finished in seconds
alternatives_rejected: select-by val_recall: objective primary is classification not retrieval

short: CLIP overfits early; VICReg weaker matching
why: Validation loss rose after epoch 11 while training loss kept falling
decision: clip_mlp_d32: best epoch 11 of 31 (early stop), val loss 3.27, val R@1 0.137 vs initial 0.004; overfitting pattern. vicreg_mlp_d32: best epoch 59 of 79, val R@1 0.053. Both well above chance (0.0006). Next: regularised CLIP iteration.
alternatives_rejected: accept as is: overfitting rule says add dropout/wd

why: First CLIP run overfit quickly; more dropout may generalise better
decision: clip_mlp_d32_reg: dropout 0.3, weight decay 1e-3, hidden 128, max 3 min (budget total 8+5+3+3 baselines = 19 of 20)

why: It scored highest on fine cell types and matched cells best
decision: On val, clip_mlp_d32_reg is chosen as the primary joint model: label_fine probe 0.900 vs RNA alone 0.849, ATAC alone 0.818, early fusion 0.880, clip_mlp_d32 0.832, vicreg 0.868; R@5 0.276/0.265, FOSCTTM 0.024. vicreg kept as alternative on test (best atac->rna r 0.475). rna->atac per-cell AUROC 0.672 vs train-mean 0.661 for all models: weak. No more iterations; budget used 19 of 20 min. Test run on rna_only, atac_only, early_fusion, clip_mlp_d32_reg, vicreg.
alternatives_rejected: clip_mlp_d32 (overfit, lower probe), vicreg (weaker matching, lower fine probe)

short: Cell-type probe and cross-modal prediction on test
why: These are the two tasks the objective named
decision: Test: label_fine probe bal-acc joint CLIP-reg 0.884 [0.858,0.908] vs RNA alone 0.831, ATAC alone 0.833, early fusion 0.849 (chance 0.059); paired diff vs RNA +0.053 [+0.016,+0.086], vs ATAC +0.051 [+0.012,+0.093], vs early fusion +0.035 [-0.001,+0.074]. Coarse label 0.983 vs 0.977/0.951/0.976 (vs RNA +0.006 [-0.012,+0.025]). Weakest large class: Tcm/Naive helper T (573 test cells) recall 0.613. Prediction atac->rna per-cell r: CLIP-reg 0.466, vicreg 0.476, ATAC-alone 0.457, train-mean 0.300; per-feature r 0.118, 13.5% of genes r>0.3. rna->atac per-cell AUROC 0.671 vs train-mean 0.661 (per-feature 0.597 vs 0.5): barely above baseline. Retrieval (extra): FOSCTTM 0.024 (chance 0.5), R@5 0.28 (chance 0.003).

short: Use regularised CLIP joint embedding; multimodal helps
why: It beats each single modality on fine cell types, with CI above zero
decision: Verdict: Multimodal helps (fine cell types only). Recommend clip_mlp_d32_reg joint embedding for cell-type annotation (+0.053 vs RNA, +0.051 vs ATAC, CIs exclude 0; vs early fusion +0.035, CI includes 0, so simple PCA concat is a near-equal, simpler option). For atac->rna prediction, ATAC alone ridge is nearly as good (0.457 vs 0.466; tiny gain); rna->atac not usefully predictable. Caveats: labels predicted from RNA (CellTypist), one donor, rare classes <10 test cells, kmeans ARI lower than baselines. Would change: a test gain vs early fusion with CI excluding 0, or labels not derived from RNA.
alternatives_rejected: early_fusion_pca: CI vs clip includes 0; vicreg: no probe gain
